observations.result: Read-only Worker inspected the owned memory and had no command method; write Worker corrected content and pinned it. Reusing the pre-correction revision returned memory/conflict. Importance, evidence count, kind and scope remained unchanged.

Declining forget returned changed=false and kept the record. Approved correction committed with origin=agent. A user correction injected during approval made the Agent commit reject memory/conflict, preserving the user change. Approval answers were fixture-driven, not a real model or native chat approval click.

observations.case: Compiled plugin SQLite fault and retry
observations.result: Targeted BEFORE UPDATE trigger on the owned memory rejected the actual Memory Desk correction form. Draft text remained, exactly one localized database error appeared, old content stayed Concurrent user correction and domain-event count remained 5. Trigger removed in finally; the same form retried successfully and displayed corrected content.

While a correction form was open with a new draft, the production Agent tool committed another correction. Submitting the old plugin form displayed memoryConflict localized text and retained the draft. Back then Refresh showed the actual Agent content; no automatic rebase occurred.

Submitting the forget form with unchecked confirmation displayed Required and did not mutate. After checking confirmation and submitting, Personal memory showed No memories found; Worker inspect returned null. SQLite retained status=forgotten and original event history.

Owned event sequence before cleanup: promoted/agent, revised/plugin:capability-memory-feedback-write, feedback/same plugin, revised/agent, revised/user, revised/plugin:capability-memory-domain-desk, revised/agent, forgotten/plugin:capability-memory-domain-desk. Cleanup appended another user forgotten event rather than deleting log history.

unitEvidence: Rust read snapshot combines serialized active row with latest locally appended memory event ID; equal-millisecond ABA changes revision. Immediate transaction validates condition, appends/applies event and outbox, computes receipt, then commits.

Rust tests cover correction/pin/unpin/forget, missing/inactive rows, extra scope/weight/evidence fields, unsupported event types and signals, SQL rejection rollback of log/projection/outbox, and retry.

TS tests cover exact bounded copied inputs, Agent approval/decline/wrong-book/extra fields/concurrent writer, read-only plugin actions, captured form revision, invalid input and conflict propagation. Follow-up tests verify arguments cannot change the approved operation and cancellation before inspection or during approval prevents mutation.

boundaries: Revision is device-local, not a cross-device CAS or an approval token. Write grant permits all memory scopes; book Agent limits other-book access before approval.

Mutation cancellation is checked before IPC dispatch; a dispatched durable write may finish and is not undone. No new observe stream or public write to scope, weights, evidence counts or raw projections.
Forget suppresses active retrieval, not physical deletion of events, prior prompts or external copies. There is no public restore operation.

Legacy automatic consolidation/reinforcement writes do not yet use these expectedRevision tokens; their stale-plan protection is not proved. Legacy correct/reject feedback signals still have no projection effect and are not exposed by mutate.
No complete packaged/Windows/Linux, consent upgrade flow, all-format, real chat approval UI, autonomous inference or multi-device campaign was verified. Existing native/bridge/build warnings remain.
